title: Smooth-functorial normalized toric desingularization over the rationals
statement: For fine torsion-free monoschemes $M$ with finite affine covers, write $X=\mathbf Q[M]$ and use normalized towers in [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. There exists one rule $\mathcal F$ on all these toric schemes, also including finite disjoint unions, such that $\mathcal F(X)$ is a finite normalized blowup tower $X_n\to\cdots\to X_0=X$. Each center is a coherent ring ideal $J_i$ whose closed zero scheme is nonempty and nowhere dense, and $X_n$ is regular. For every smooth $\mathbf Q$-morphism $h:Y\to X$ between toric schemes in this family, $\mathcal F(Y)$ is canonically the contraction of $h^*\mathcal F(X)$, with the pulled-back ideals retained in their order; for surjective $h$ no stage is contracted. These identifications respect identities and composition. At every stage the torus action of each connected toric component of $X$ extends to $X_i$ and preserves $J_i$.

source.place: Expose VIII, Theorem 2.3.10, normalized restriction in 2.3.9 and Remark 2.3.12(i), equivariance in Corollary 2.3.17, printed pp.93--95; application in 3.2.19, p.106. No Stacks tag states this monoidal-geometric result.

proof.text: Choose one ordinary smooth-functorial resolution rule $R$ on all reduced finite-type $\mathbf Q$-schemes, including finite disjoint unions, by [lem-trf-smooth-functorial-ordinary-resolution]. Apply [lem-trf-normalized-resolution-on-normal-inputs] to this rule. It gives $N=R^\nu$ on normal inputs, with coherent nonempty nowhere dense centers, regular last level, and the required ordered smooth-pullback contractions and coherence laws.

Apply [lem-trf-conductor-extension-of-normalized-resolution] to $N$. This supplies the explicit rule $H=H_N$ on all reduced finite-type rational schemes by the initial conductor normalized blowup followed by the normal-input rule. Its statement gives the tower, center and terminal-regularity clauses and every smooth-comparison, identity, composition and surjectivity clause, including the valid omission of a unit conductor stage.

source.place: Retained steps 3--4; conductor refinement of ILO VIII 2.2.3--2.2.9 and 2.3.4--2.3.5(i).

proof.text: By [lem-trf-toric-realization-finite-type], every required $X=\mathbf Q[M]$, including finite disjoint unions, is reduced of finite type. Restrict $H$ to these inputs and put $\mathcal F(X)=H(X)$. The comparisons just obtained apply to every smooth scheme morphism between them, so give all the stated tower and functoriality clauses with the normalized-tower conventions of [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization].

Fix a connected component of $X$. Its torus is a finite-rank split torus by [lem-trf-toric-realization-finite-type]. Extend its action by the identity on the other components; these finitely many components are open and closed. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-functorial-tower-torus-equivariance] to this action and to the rule $H$ on the larger family of all reduced finite-type schemes. Its uncontracted projection/action comparison and lifting conclusion give actions on every level, equivariant transitions and equality of the action and projection pullbacks of each center ideal. This is precisely the invariance required by [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. Do this for each component torus; the tower is always the same $H(X)$, so the choices are synchronized.

proof_origin.place: Expose VIII 2.2.4--2.2.9, 2.3.9--2.3.17 and 3.2.19; initial conductor-stage refinement to make unit-stage contraction literal on nonnormal inputs.
